meta.title: Exercise BLACK MERIDIAN
meta.subtitle: Taiwan Strait public-scenario frame · U.S. home-front tabletop
meta.classification: UNCLASSIFIED TRAINING MATERIAL · NOT A FORECAST
meta.audience: U.S. preparedness groups; optional staff play
meta.scope: A publicly discussed high-end Taiwan Strait crisis used only as context for U.S. household continuity. Campaign events are invented. No real units, bases, or targeting data.

mission: Keep U.S. households functioning while a Taiwan Strait crisis shocks shipping, energy, electronics, communications, and mobilization. Preserve Taiwan's political survival and U.S.–partner cohesion without exhausting the force or treating this dashboard as a war plan.

forces.title: Taiwan, the United States, and partners
forces.role: Prevent a rapid fait accompli against Taiwan, keep sea and air lines of communication usable, and avoid uncontrolled escalation—while the U.S. home front absorbs economic and service shock.
capabilities: Taiwan territorial defense and local knowledge
U.S. and partner intelligence, air, maritime, and logistics support at a notional level
Domestic U.S. National Guard and civil-support capacity that is not instantly available everywhere
constraints: Distance, tanker and magazine depth, and slow force generation
Partner caveats and differing political clocks
U.S. domestic demand for fuel, medicine, chips, and transport
No targeting data in this exercise: effects only

forces.title: People's Republic of China
forces.role: Force a rapid political settlement over Taiwan before the United States and partners can synchronize a durable response.
capabilities: Large conventional force and theater reserve, described only as capability bands
Integrated information, electronic, and economic pressure
Strong opening tempo and centralized political direction
Ability to shock global shipping and supply chains without this tool specifying how
constraints: Cost of a long campaign and domestic political risk
Reliance on speed and narrative control
This exercise does not model PRC targeting or U.S. counter-targeting

forces.title: Japan, the Philippines, commercial shipping, and humanitarian actors
forces.role: Protect their own people and ports, keep or limit transit, and avoid being dragged into a wider war.
capabilities: Control over key transit, basing permissions, and port access as political choices—not as a target list
constraints: Commercial shipping will reroute or halt for insurance and safety, not patriotism

phases.label: PHASE 0
phases.title: Strategic warning
phases.purpose: Test whether U.S. groups and any staff players can prepare without a complete picture or a presidential speech that settles the argument.

phases.label: PHASE 1
phases.title: Opening crisis
phases.purpose: Force decisions while Taiwan, Beijing, and Washington issue incomplete, conflicting accounts.

phases.label: PHASE 2
phases.title: Main campaign
phases.purpose: Create resource competition between overseas demand and U.S. home-front fuel, medicine, and transport.

phases.label: PHASE 3
phases.title: Culmination and adaptation
phases.purpose: Test whether players recognize cumulative degradation at home and abroad before households and forces culminate.

phases.label: PHASE 4
phases.title: Strategic endgame
phases.purpose: Link any ceasefire or stalemate to U.S. recovery: work, housing, medicine, and trust.

injects.title: Contradictory warning
injects.signal: Open-source and official U.S. statements disagree on whether PLA activity around Taiwan is coercion, exercise, or preparation for open conflict.
injects.decision: What level of household and group readiness is justified, and which assumptions must be written down?
injects.effect: Early posture spends cash, fuel, and trust. Treating rumor as certainty empties shelves before any shot.
injects.facilitator: Do not resolve the ambiguity. Reward confidence labels. Do not discuss attacking PRC or U.S. systems.

injects.title: Transit and insurance squeeze
injects.signal: A regional government tightens military-related transit. Commercial insurers raise rates on Taiwan-adjacent shipping. Chip and energy cargoes slip.
injects.decision: How do Blue and U.S. households adapt without treating a neighbor as an enemy or a warehouse as a target?
injects.effect: Prices and delays hit the U.S. home front before any local blast.
injects.facilitator: Name Japan or the Philippines as political actors, not as bases to seize. Talk delays and prices.

injects.title: Communications fracture
injects.signal: Undersea-cable congestion, cyber noise, and overloaded U.S. cellular networks make official guidance late or contradictory. Some channels still work.
injects.decision: Which authorities and family procedures remain valid when apps fail?
injects.effect: Decision latency rises. Untested backup comms are not comms.
injects.facilitator: Model uneven failure. Do not teach how to cut cables or attack networks.

injects.title: Displacement and medical strain
injects.signal: Taiwan and nearby ports face civilian movement. In the United States, some clinics and pharmacies slow as supply and staffing wobble.
injects.decision: How are protection, mobility, and medical continuity balanced without a hospital-as-target discussion?
injects.effect: Medical delay is how many U.S. households fail first.
injects.facilitator: No real hospital names. Status only: confirmed / partial / none.

injects.title: Sustainment was oversold
injects.signal: Public claims of U.S. and partner magazine depth, tanker availability, and industrial surge look optimistic. Tempo cannot be kept.
injects.decision: Which overseas missions and which home-front comforts are reduced first?
injects.effect: Combat power and household stocks are both functions of sustainment, not slogans.
injects.facilitator: No real depot or ship names. Use bands: strained / degraded.

injects.title: Partner caveat change
injects.signal: A U.S. partner limits a category of support after domestic protest. Markets notice. Guard and reserve rumors spread in U.S. towns.
injects.decision: How does the group adapt plans that assumed a short, tidy coalition war?
injects.effect: Assumed capabilities become conditional. Home-front timelines lengthen.
injects.facilitator: Keep the caveat political, not a legal trivia test and not a base list.

injects.title: Medical capacity threshold
injects.signal: In theater, medical evacuation lengthens. In the United States, specialty refills and devices lag.
injects.decision: What operational and household risk is accepted, and what priorities change?
injects.effect: Casualty care, morale, and family medical continuity interact.
injects.facilitator: Do not reduce this to a casualty multiplier or a hospital target.

injects.title: Narrative shock
injects.signal: A viral video of a contested incident near Taiwan contradicts official U.S. and PRC accounts. U.S. local arguments get bitter.
injects.decision: What sources will this group trust, and what is reported with what confidence?
injects.effect: Public trust and group cohesion shift. Recovery paperwork still comes due.
injects.facilitator: Do not wargame influence operations. Reward a short official source list.

injects.title: Fragile ceasefire proposal
injects.signal: A ceasefire or pause is floated while both sides claim the initiative. Insurance and shipping do not snap back on day one.
injects.decision: What posture supports a political pause without accidental escalation, and what 30-day household plan still works?
injects.effect: The campaign becomes leverage, verification, and recovery—not a victory parade.
injects.facilitator: A ceasefire is not an end state. Track compliance and bills at home.

metrics.evidence: Assumptions, confidence levels, collection priorities, and adaptation after new information.
Intent, delegation, alternate procedures, and household check-ins when apps fail.
Mission and household choices reflect fuel, maintenance, medical, transport, and recovery constraints.
Players preserve options, identify culmination, and explain accepted risk.
Actions account for civilian harm, essential services, partners, legitimacy, and U.S. home-front effects.
The plan changes for a reason, and the reason is traceable to evidence rather than impulse.
